howto.goal: Be the last player with dice. Bid on how many of one face are on the whole table, or call the last bid a lie.
howto.setup: Each player rolls five hidden dice and sees only their own. Everyone starts with five dice.

sections.title: Bidding
sections.text: A bid says a face and a count, for example three fours. Each new bid must raise the count or the face.

sections.title: Calling a lie
sections.text: If you think the bid is too high, call it. Everyone shows their dice. Whoever is wrong loses one die.

sections.title: Winning
sections.text: The last player holding dice wins the game.

controls: Click a bid button to raise the count or the face.
Click Call the bid a lie to challenge the last bid.
Use the table chat to talk before you bid — talking is part of the game.

frames.say: Your five dice are hidden from everyone else.
You can see three fours here. Bid on fours.

demo.intro: A round played out, with the bid and the challenge named.

frames.say: Four players each roll five dice and look only at their own.
The first player bids two threes.
The next player raises it to three threes.
A third player is not convinced and calls the bid a lie.
Everyone shows their dice. There are only two threes, so the bidder loses a die.

demo.outro: Count what you can see, and bid one higher than you believe the table holds.

steps.say: Look at your own dice and count the faces you hold most of.
Make a low, safe bid to start — two of a face you actually hold.
Raise the bid only when you hold more of that face yourself.
Call a lie when the count asked for is more than you think the table can hold.
